root_idea.summary: A distinguishing mark or trace by which something is recognized; from this develop knowing, making known, signs and landmarks, and the worlds as distinguishable classes of creation.
root_idea.development: The root moves from a mark that identifies a thing to recognition and knowledge, then to teaching or making knowledge available. Its world-sense reflects classes of creation understood as signs of their Maker.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Normalized Form II perfect citation form.
Normalized Form V perfect citation form.
Presented under the singular citation form عَلَم for the Quranic plural أَعْلَام.
Presented under the singular citation form عَالَم for the Quranic plural عَالَمِينَ.
Presented under the singular citation form عَلَامَة for the Quranic plural عَلَامَات.
Normalized citation form عَلِيم; the QAC group also contains its Quranic plural عُلَمَاء.
Inflected feminine plural of the same passive participle; normalized under مَعْلُوم.

senses.definition: To know, recognize, or be acquainted with something.
senses.usage_conditions: Normally takes one object; the Quran also uses it for knowing or recognizing persons and things, including knowledge acquired or realized in a situation.

senses.definition: To know or judge that something is or is not the case; to ascertain something with certainty.
senses.usage_conditions: May take two objective complements, especially in constructions equivalent to “know someone to be …”; grammatical aspect, voice, and subject do not create separate lexical senses.

senses.definition: To teach, instruct, or impart knowledge to someone.
senses.usage_conditions: Typically takes a learner and the knowledge, text, skill, or matter taught; repeated or sustained instruction may be emphasized, but the active and passive forms belong to the same lexical sense.
The form may be used transitively or intransitively; it presents knowledge as acquired by the learner rather than imparted by a teacher.

senses.definition: A distinguishing mark, landmark, or prominent mountain used as a sign.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural أَعْلَام refers to large, conspicuous mountain-like landmarks in the sea; the lexical branch also covers markers and signs by which places or things are recognized.

senses.definition: More knowing, most knowing, or knowing best.
senses.usage_conditions: Used comparatively or superlatively; in expressions concerning God, the context may mean that God knows best or simply that God knows.

senses.definition: A world, realm, or class of created beings; collectively, the worlds or creation.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural عَالَمِينَ denotes the created worlds or classes of creation. Classical interpretation varies over whether it emphasizes all creatures, intelligent creatures, or distinct kinds such as humans, jinn, and angels.

senses.definition: A knower or learned person, one possessing knowledge.
senses.usage_conditions: Applied to human beings or other knowers; the Quranic plural may refer to learned people or knowers.

senses.definition: The Knower, whose knowledge leaves nothing hidden.
senses.usage_conditions: When used as a divine description, it denotes comprehensive knowledge rather than an acquired human state.

senses.definition: A sign, mark, token, or indication by which something is recognized.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural عَلَامَات refers to visible signs or landmarks used for orientation; the sense is not restricted to any particular object class.

senses.definition: Very knowing, learned, or possessing knowledge to a high degree.
senses.usage_conditions: Can describe a human being as learned or knowledgeable; the Quranic group also contains the plural عُلَمَاء, “scholars.”
As a divine epithet, it denotes knowledge of what has been and will be, encompassing what is hidden and manifest, small and great.
This sense is represented by the Quranic plural form عُلَمَاء within the supplied QAC grouping; it denotes people distinguished by knowledge.

senses.definition: Supremely knowing; all-knowing, especially of hidden matters.
senses.usage_conditions: An intensive description used in the Quran for comprehensive divine knowledge, including knowledge of the unseen; it is not merely a grammatical intensifier in these contexts.

senses.definition: Knowledge, understanding, or awareness of a thing as it truly is.
senses.usage_conditions: May be theoretical or practical, rational or received, and may concern ordinary or specially granted knowledge; the noun is the opposite of ignorance.

senses.definition: Knowledge understood as action according to what is known.
senses.usage_conditions: Reported for the Quranic context of 12:68; the primary sense “knowledge” remains the more direct interpretation there.

senses.definition: Taught or instructed; one who has been taught.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is a passive participle of عَلَّمَ; the identity of the teacher or the subject taught is supplied by context.
The Quranic plural مَعْلُومَات is used of specified or appointed times or days; مَعْلُوم may also describe a fixed term, portion, or determinate matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To possess knowledge as a firmly rooted faculty; to be learned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive stative use distinct from the ordinary transitive verb عَلِمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To try, test, or prove someone and thereby ascertain his condition or qualities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Found in the expression عَلِمْتُ عِلْمَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To use عَلِمَ as a verb of swearing or asseveration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can introduce a similarly complemented assertion; يَعْلَمُ اللهُ is likewise used as an asseverative formula.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compete with someone in knowledge and surpass him in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III verbal construction concerning rivalry in knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mark, brand, or place a distinguishing sign on something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes marking a garment, book, object, or person; the mark may identify or distinguish the marked thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slit the upper lip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily action distinct from the knowledge and marking branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a fissure or cleft in the upper lip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or camel; the fissure may be in the lip generally or on one side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give a garment, book, horse, grave, or person a mark, border, badge, or identifying sign.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes decorative or embroidered borders, a mark placed on writing, a war badge, and a tombstone used as a marker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a well-digger, to find that the well contains abundant water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For water, to flow over the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use of the Form VIII verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For lightning, to shine or gleam.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in a poetic expression concerning lightning seen on or near a mountain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or desire someone to tell or inform one about something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Typically used with news or information as the requested object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A predominant or preponderant opinion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A secondary use in which strong belief stands in place of fully established knowledge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first thing, or before everything else.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Found in the idiom لَقِيتُهُ أَدْنَى عِلْمٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impression, footprint, track, or trace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The identifying trace left by a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The ornamental, figured, variegated, or embroidered border of a garment or cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A textile sense; its plural is أَعْلَام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A waymark or erected object used to guide travelers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be a structure, sign, or other prominent object in a road or desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A boundary or separation between two lands.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes marked limits such as the boundaries of a sacred territory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A banner or military standard around which soldiers gather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May also refer to a strip of cloth tied to a spear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief or prominent leader of a people or group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from a mountain or banner as a conspicuous marker.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fissure in the upper lip or in one side of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun corresponding to the harelipped branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Related to knowledge or science; scientific or theoretical.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with عَمَلِيّ, practical or action-oriented.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variant pronunciation or substitution for غُلَام, a boy or youth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported consonant substitution rather than a knowledge-derived meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark, sign, token, characteristic, symptom, or indication by which a person or thing is known.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote either a concrete badge or a distinguishing feature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, active, sharp, or acute-minded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man; this is a separate lexical item from the intensive adjective عَلَّام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A very skilled genealogist or person possessing exceptional knowledge of genealogies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive human specialization of the knowledge branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hawk, especially a sparrow-hawk or goshawk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A homonymous lexical branch with its own animal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Henna, the plant used for dyeing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The marking sense is understood through the use of henna as a coloring mark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The kernel of the stone of the lote fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A generation or the people of one period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A secondary nominal use equivalent to قَرْن.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well or body of abundant water, including the sea or water concealed beneath the earth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote a deep, broad, salty, copious, or subterranean body of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large cooking pot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Plump and soft, tender, or delicate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A frog.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported animal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A male hyena, described as large-bellied or swollen at the sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare animal description preserved as an independent lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coat of mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare, verse-attested noun distinct from the feminine of أَعْلَم.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or object where the existence of something is known or can be recognized.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may describe a person known to possess a quality, as well as a place that reveals or indicates something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sign, trace, or indicator by which one finds or is guided to a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a road marker and an indication associated with an approaching event; the latter Quran citation is not assigned to a modern location here.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An indication or symptom of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the guiding-sign sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Marked or bearing a mark, as a garment, cloth, or gaming arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive participle of أَعْلَمَ in its marking sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who marks or gives a sign, including one who displays a badge or sign of war.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participle of أَعْلَمَ; includes marking a garment and distinguishing oneself in battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Directed by inspiration toward what is right and good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized passive-participial use beyond the ordinary meaning “taught.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A teacher or instructor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary agent noun of عَلَّمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A title of address for a Christian or a Jew.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later conventional title, distinct from the general occupational sense “teacher.”

lane_unit_coverage.note: Knowledge, recognition, certainty, and objective-complement constructions.

Generation or people of one period.

cautions: The QAC group for عَلِيم also contains the plural عُلَمَاء; that materially distinct plural usage is represented as a separate numbered sense under the normalized عَلِيم entry.

Some English renderings of Form I عَلِمَ, especially “make evident,” reflect contextual or interpretive readings of knowledge becoming manifest; they have not been promoted to a separate lexical sense without independent lexical evidence.
Lane's historical Quran citations have been used only as lexical evidence; no unverified modern verse location has been assigned to them.
